intro: Truck drivers control heavy equipment, monitor conditions and keep tight schedules, skills that rail and construction value. The closest of the 25 careers below is rail yard engineering, with an 88% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $60,600, which is 3% more than the $58,640 truck drivers earn.
why_it_works: Long hauls mean watching gauges, reading the road and fixing small problems before they stop you. O*NET rates operation and control and operations monitoring at 3.75 out of 5 for this job. Rail, mining and construction equipment jobs use the same control skills, often closer to home. Almost every match needs no new schooling. The gaps are teaching, leading people and complex problem solving.
tips: Your CDL and safety record are your best assets; list miles driven and years without incidents.
Locomotive Engineers earn $81,410, which is 39% more, and railroads train new hires.
Underground mining machine operators earn $74,500, or 27% more, if you can work shifts underground.

faq.q: What jobs can former truck drivers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are rail yard engineers and hostlers (88%), tank car, truck and ship loaders (86%) and refuse collectors (85%), based on O*NET 31.0. Construction equipment operators are 82% matched and earn $59,850, which is 2% more than truck drivers earn.

faq.q: Which careers for truck drivers pay more?
faq.a: 15 of the 25 matches pay more than the $58,640 median. Subway and Streetcar Operators earn $86,380 (47% more), Locomotive Engineers $81,410 (39% more) and mining roof bolters $78,540 (34% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Rail jobs also tend to keep you closer to home.

faq.q: Do truck drivers need a degree to change careers?
faq.a: No. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than truck drivers already have, including all of the top 10. In the closest match, 83% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and employers train on the job.

faq.q: What skills should truck drivers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are instructing, managing people, complex problem solving and coordination. Troubleshooting already rates 3 out of 5 for truck drivers in O*NET, so training new drivers or leading a crew is the usual step toward higher pay.
